subject: Streaming chat: sudden p99 queue buildup during peak traffic - customer escalation
messages:
From: Rajiv Chopra <rajiv@peakflow.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted chat stream during peak (details attached)

Hi Logan,

We started seeing sustained p95/p99 spikes on the hosted streaming chat endpoint between 06:30-07:10 PDT yesterday and again during today's evening peak. The UX impact: several sessions stalled for ~8-12s before the next chunk arrived, and a few websocket clients reconnected.

Key data:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1.9k
- Error-rate increase: 0.6% -> 1.8% across the period
- p99 latency (SSE chunk delivery): baseline ~220ms, spiked to 3.1s

I attached the stream logs and a short runner script that reproduces the load pattern we used. We're seeing the stalls primarily on the /v1/stream/chat endpoint. We're on the hosted API in us-west with model pinned to rdx-large-v2.

This started impacting our customers at ~06:35 PDT and we had to shift some traffic off the streaming route to the polling fallback. Can you confirm whether this is on your side or something we did? We can hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Chopra
VP Engineering, PeakFlow AI
attachments: stream-logs-0913.zip (zip), perf-graphs-0913.png (png)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted chat stream during peak (details attached)

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the data and the reproduction script. We're looking into this with SRE and the runtime team now. Initial acknowledgment: we see elevated tail latency in our monitoring that overlaps the windows you called out.

Immediate next steps we're running:
- Hannah is pulling traces and the streaming router traces for the affected time windows.
- We'll analyze KV cache hit/miss rates and any queuing at the frontend proxies.
- If we need to, we can temporarily route your production traffic to a higher-tier pool (larger instance class) while we stabilize.

Marissa, I'll let you coordinate customer comms and keep Rajiv updated on timeline. Rajiv, could you confirm the traffic pattern in the repro (burst size and inter-message gap)? That will help us match the workload.

I'll update within 2 hours with an initial triage.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes — traces pulled and initial findings

FW: Rajiv's logs attached. I pulled the streaming router traces and SLO traces for 06:20-07:30 PDT. Highlights:

- We observed short periods where inbound request bursts caused the frontend queue length to climb above our target of 350 for ~40s windows.
- During queue climbs, we see an increase in per-request scheduling latency (scheduler wait) -> downstream stall while KV cache warmed.
- Error lines in traces: "backend_write_timeout" (n=7) and "session-heartbeat-missed" (n=12) — these correspond to long-tail chunk delays.

I'm attaching the SLO trace dump (slo-traces-0913.txt). It shows repeated small batches where the worker reused KV entries but missed prefix cache hits due to eviction churn. That causes a sequence of longer model-internal attention prep steps and yields the 2–3s p99 spikes Rajiv reported.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Increase frontend per-route max_queue_size from 350 -> 600 for BrightCommerce routes for the next 24h.
2) Increase the per-connection keepalive to avoid client reconnects during short stalls.
3) Temporarily route BrightCommerce to a higher-memory worker class to reduce eviction churn.

I agree with Logan's suggestion to consider a temporary routing bump while we stabilize. Rishi, can you run a quick sim of increasing cache capacity for the rdx-large-v2 variant and share perf deltas?

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: slo-traces-0913.txt (text)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 11:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Investigation notes — queue buildup and KV eviction hypothesis

I ran a focused sim against the same pattern Rajiv sent (1.9k concurrent connections with 200–400 msg/s bursts and a 250ms inter-message gap). Results:

- Baseline rdx-large-v2 w/ default cache: p99 = 2.9s under burst
- Increase cache-max-entries by 2x: p99 drops to ~520ms (significant improvement)
- Increase frontend max_queue_size to 600: reduces scheduler wait events by ~58% in sim
- Temporarily routing to rdx-large-x1 (higher memory) gives p99 ~360ms in sim but doubles per-hour cost.

Root cause: eviction churn in the KV/prefix cache when many short-lived sessions start/stop in tight bursts. The streaming path has a small scheduling window; when the queue backs up it amplifies the eviction effect.

Recommended immediate plan (order matters):
A) Apply frontend max_queue_size=600 and increase keepalive to 45s (low risk, fast rollback).
B) Apply a temporary cache-max-entries increase for BrightCommerce model variants for 6–12 hours.
C) If traffic remains unstable, fail traffic to higher-tier pool (rdx-large-x1) for 24 hours.

I'll open INF-4921 with the sim outputs and attach kv-metrics.csv and investigation-notes.md so we have a reproducible record.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
attachments: kv-metrics.csv, investigation-notes.md

Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming chat: sudden p99 queue buildup during peak traffic - customer escalation (next steps & timeline)

Hi team — quick summary and actions after the triage run:

Summary:
- Cause: KV prefix cache eviction churn under tight bursty session patterns which amplified frontend scheduler wait leading to p99 spikes.
- Scope: BrightCommerce production routes in us-west only; estimated affected sessions ~1.9k concurrent.

Immediate actions (we executed A already):
1) Frontend max_queue_size increased to 600 for BrightCommerce routes (rolled at 02:20 UTC 2028-09-14) — observed immediate reduction in scheduling waits.
2) Keepalive increased to 45s to reduce reconnect churn.
3) Rishi applied a temporary cache-max-entries bump for the rdx-large-v2 variant for BrightCommerce for 12 hours.

Observed outcome: p99 dropped from ~3.1s -> ~460ms in monitoring post-mitigation. Error rates returned near baseline.

Next (by EOD):
- If we see any recurrence during the next two peak windows, we will fail traffic to rdx-large-x1 for a 24-hour stability window (we will give 30 minutes notice).
- Hannah will follow up with a postmortem including root cause and a durable fix (likely a cache tuning + adaptive queue controller) by 2028-09-20.
- Marissa & Aditya: coordinate commercial follow-up w/ BrightCommerce procurement on SLA credit and any temporary cost uplift; CC me on threads.

Ticket: JIRA INF-4921 (tracked internally). Drive folder with logs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/brightcommerce/peakflow-0913-logs

We're keeping this on high priority until the next two peak windows pass. Rajiv, thanks again for the clear repro — that materially sped up diagnosis.

—Logan
